notes: ARRI Orbiter is an LED lighting fixture (point-source luminaire), not a traditional AV signal-chain device, so category/type were set to "other" — no better fit exists in the given enum. Physical I/O per ARRI's official data sheet (Feb 2024, Ident.-No. 80.0033506) and the "Control & Connectivity" / "Tech Specs" pages at arri.com/en/lighting/led-spotlights/orbiter: mains powerCON TRUE1 TOP in; 3-pin XLR DC battery in (48-52V); two 5-pin XLR DMX ports (in and thru, daisy-chainable, also carry RDM E1.20); two EtherCON ports (in and thru, daisy-chainable, Art-Net 4/sACN/TCP-IP) — no link-speed (100M/1G) is stated in the datasheet so no "grade" was set; two USB-A ports (LiOS firmware updates via USB stick, third-party peripherals e.g. Wi-Fi dongles); one USB-C port (PC communication/servicing). Two additional physical features are documented but omitted from the port list because no connector id in the allowed taxonomy fits them: an SD-card slot (firmware/software expansion) and a dedicated camera "sync input" port for frame-accurate flashing (connector type not disclosed in any source checked, including B&H and Newsshooter's review — likely a small proprietary or mini-jack connector). The removable Control Panel accessory connects "via PoE" per the datasheet; this is not broken out as a separate physical port since ARRI's own port list does not distinguish it from the EtherCON ports. No SDI/HDMI/video ports exist on this fixture (it is lighting-only). Also has built-in wireless DMX (LumenRadio CRMX) which is not a physical port.

ports.name: DC In (Battery)
ports.note: 3-pin XLR DC power input, 48-52V (Pin 1 negative, Pin 2 positive) — not an audio signal; closest taxonomy connector to a 3-pin XLR DC port is xlr3 since xlr3-dc is not in the allowed list.
